checks: All three complete current production files were read at the supplied pins. The retained shared_ptr header is byte-identical to the current pinned toolchain header, SHA 3241AF290FC414E0228B5312656A4AFBE11B7DE9ED9D09E80A97FAB6E8DC4293.

Storage size/alignment report the real PiNodePermission. construct starts AllocationScope before placement-new; destroy invokes the real object destructor but never frees caller-owned placement storage.

Original construction order is retained: FSPermission (with two actual root Nodes) then ChildProcess, Worker, Inspector, WASI and Addon, followed by three filesystem and five distinct policy map insertions.

The pinned make_shared delegates to allocate_shared. Each new call uses the same actual __shared_ptr_emplace<Derived, Allocator<Derived>> with the ordinary no-argument allocator_traits construct path; __construct_at ultimately uses Derived(), retaining value initialization of the implicit five simple policy constructors.

Converting and moving shared_ptr<Derived> to shared_ptr<PermissionBase> keeps the same control block. Final release invokes allocator_traits destruction of Derived, not delete through the non-virtual PermissionBase destructor. The control-block weak release then uses the rebound custom allocator.

Node new routes the actual requested size through allocateStandard; delete routes its exact pointer to the prefix release owner. Prefixes retain their memory owner separately. Map, String, vector and control-block deallocation use that same original prefix and do not depend on the current TLS domain.

The active AllocationScope retains the caller's domain through synchronous construction/materialization/queries and restores its predecessor on return. Each successful block separately retains its domain, so destruction can occur after allocation scope/runtime/caller domain entitlement retirement.

C ABI Apply materializes an actual vector of copied Strings under its operation scope, then passes a synchronous borrowed Environment view. These copies retire before AllocationScope. is_granted passes only a synchronous string_view. No Environment, JSContext, Path/Map, trace, debug function table, or caller resource pointer is stored in Permission or policy/node fields.

The internal ABI requires live/aligned placement storage, nonnull memory owner and valid borrowed inputs for the selected operation. It is not a checked public interface and makes no JS owner or full Environment installation claim.

The established standard allocator requires the pinned no-C++-exceptions build and preserves its native new_handler/bad_alloc terminal policy; this review does not add a recoverable constructor-failure or JS OOM mapping.
